archetype.name: Rebuilding (defense ahead of offense)
archetype.definition: A team in its fourth straight losing season whose defense has stabilized while an injury-thinned roster cannot score, so the losses keep coming.

report.headline: A competent-looking defense chained to the league's second-worst offense, and a frontcourt in street clothes.
report.take:
Utah is 1-13, on a 12-game losing streak and has lost all of its last ten. This is the fourth straight bad season after 17-65 and 22-60, so the losing is not a shock. What has changed is the shape of it. The defense, last in defensive rating two years running and 29th last year, sits 24th at 117.6, and its shot profile looks respectable: opponents post a 52.5 Opp eFG % (10th) and take only 26.8% of their shots at the rim (8th). The collapse is on the other end. A 106.7 offensive rating ranks 29th, 7.5 points below the league, and last season's offense was a league-average-ish 114.1.

The offense is broken at the most basic level: making shots. Utah's eFG % of 50.8 is 29th and its TS % is 28th, while it attempts a slightly below-average share of threes and makes them at 33.8%. The lead creators aren't efficient. Darryn Peterson is at 52.4 TS % on 24.7 USG %, and Keyonte George carries a 28.8 USG % at 55.0 TS % with a negative BPM. Behind them, Josh Okogie, Josh Green and Svi Mykhailiuk (39.0 TS %) are giving real minutes with almost no scoring value. Add a 14.5 TOV % (22nd), and the team rarely gets a clean look.

The numbers also hide how much of the roster is missing. Jaxson Hayes, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are all listed out. Markkanen, the best-ranked forward on his tab at 17th, has played only 8 of 14 games, and Jackson has played 4. The frontcourt's C+ grade leans on Mo Bamba (5.9 BPM, 77.8 TS %) in 195 minutes. The margin, not luck, is the story: the differential implies 3 wins, so the W vs Pt Diff of -2 says a couple of close games got away, including overtime losses to San Antonio and New Orleans. Even with those back, this is a bottom-five team.

Going forward, the defense is the part to believe in and the offense is the part to doubt, but not forever. A 29th-ranked shooting team with its best scoring forward out has room to climb once Markkanen returns. The current pace of 6 wins is too grim for a team whose margin implies more. Still, nothing here points to anything other than a season near the bottom of the West.

strengths.title: Defense keeps opponents off the rim
strengths.body: Utah allows a 52.5 Opp eFG %, 10th in the league, and keeps opponents away from the basket better than all but seven teams. That is a real change from last year's 122.3 defensive rating and an Opp Rim FG % of 71.4. Strong defensive rebounding (74.3 DRB %, 9th) finishes possessions. It should hold up, though its overall rank is dragged down by forcing almost no turnovers.

strengths.title: Bamba's efficient minutes at center
strengths.body: With Hayes and Jackson out, Mo Bamba has been the most productive player on the roster per minute: 5.9 BPM and a 77.8 TS % on low usage. He ranks 16th among centers on his tab. The sample is only 195 minutes, so the shooting will cool, but he is the frontcourt's floor while the injuries last.

concerns.title: An offense that can't shoot
concerns.body: Utah's 106.7 offensive rating is 29th, built on a 50.8 eFG % that is 29th as well. The primary ball-handlers use a lot of possessions inefficiently, and the bench guards and wings add little. This persists until shot-making improves, either through Markkanen's return or Peterson's efficiency rising toward his volume.

concerns.title: Point guards feast on Utah
concerns.body: Opposing point guards are scoring 29.93 points a game against Utah, 4.87 above their own averages, the worst mark in the league by that measure. Combined with a 12.0 Opp TOV % (26th), it explains why a defense with a good shot profile still ranks 24th. Guards are getting where they want without being pressured into mistakes.

concerns.title: The frontcourt is on the injury report
concerns.body: Markkanen, Hayes and Jackson are all out, and Markkanen has played only 8 games. That pushes minutes to players like Kyle Filipowski (-8.6 BPM). The C+ frontcourt grade overstates what is actually available on a given night.

trend.note: The record has gone from 1-5 in October to 0-8 in November, and scoring dipped from 108.67 to 105.88 a game. The margin has barely moved, though: the last five games ran at -10.2 a game, slightly better than the season. This is a consistently bad team, not a collapsing one.

weekAhead.headline: Five games, two back-to-backs, and the Lakers twice.
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with a road back-to-back at the Clippers and the Lakers. It closes with Dallas at home and a return trip to Los Angeles the next night. The Lakers are 12-2 with the league's best offense at 123.0, and that is a brutal matchup for a team scoring like Utah. The Clippers (4-8) and Phoenix (5-7) are beatable on paper, and they are the realistic chances to end the streak.

The opportunities are specific. Phoenix's defense ranks 26th and is last in the league in defensive rebounding, and Utah's best stretches come from its bigs. The Clippers give up a 69.2 Opp Rim FG %, 27th. If Utah can get to the rim against those two, it has a shot. Against the Lakers twice and a .500 Dallas team, it needs its defense at its best.

keyMatchups.title: Utah guards vs leaky point-guard defenses
keyMatchups.body: Both the Lakers and Phoenix give up big nights to point guards: 31.93 and 32.92 points a game, ranked 29th and 30th. That is an opening for George, who carries the heaviest usage on the team. If he converts it efficiently, this offense looks less hopeless for a week.

keyMatchups.title: Bamba against Phoenix's soft middle
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix allows 25.08 points a game to centers (29th) and 16.25 rebounds to them. It also grabs the lowest share of defensive rebounds in the league. That is the best spot of the week for Bamba and Utah's second-chance game.

keyMatchups.title: Containing the Lakers' offense twice
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers lead the league in eFG % and offensive rating. Utah's rim-denial defense will be tested by a team that also gets to the line at the third-highest rate. Splitting even one of those games would be a surprise.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the home games against Phoenix and Dallas end the losing streak, and who starts in the frontcourt if Markkanen, Hayes or Jackson return.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense should stay in the low-to-mid 20s, roughly where it is now and better than the last two seasons. The offense is the variable. Shooting this poorly as a team is partly roster and partly sample, and Markkanen's return would lift it, so expect some climb in offensive rating, though not to league average. The close-game luck should even out, which adds a win or two over time.

The current 6-win pace understates this team; the margin implies something closer to a mid-to-high teens win total over a full season. That still means a bottom-four finish and another year of development minutes for Peterson and Ace Bailey rather than a push for the play-in. I'd put the final win total between 15 and 21.
swingFactors: How soon Markkanen and the injured bigs return
Whether the defense can start forcing turnovers

confidence.note: Only 14 games, with three key frontcourt players missing much of them; the margin is a clearer signal than the record.
